parts:
Here is a calmer, more appropriate, supportive, not-taking-sides version that still reassures her you’re being responsible and attentive:

---

Hi Tara, thank you for reaching out. I completely understand why you’re worried. I was concerned too when I saw your message. From everything I’ve seen, Carson has seemed to be doing well here. He recently started a full-time job and has been going to church with us, so I truly wasn’t aware of anything going on beneath the surface.

As soon as I got your text this morning, I checked on him before he left for work. I asked if he was okay and if he wanted to talk, and he told me he had a moment yesterday, but that he’s fine now and heading into work. He didn’t go into detail, but he said not to worry.

I’ve tried to stay neutral because he is an adult and I want him to feel safe while he’s here, but I will be sitting down with him when he gets home so I can better understand what’s going on and make sure he has the support he needs. If it seems appropriate, I will strongly encourage him to talk with the counselor Donivan has seen, who is a very grounded, older Christian male and someone the boys trust.

Please know I care about all these boys deeply and I’m doing my best to make sure everyone here is okay. I don’t encourage estrangement from family, but at his age I can only guide him, not make decisions for him. Once I’ve had a real conversation with him today, I’ll let you know he’s safe and give you whatever update I’m able to without overstepping.  

---

If you want, I can also write a shorter, more direct version or a slightly firmer boundary-setting version.

I have a 24-year-old kid that's my 17-year-old's best friend living with me in my home. He randomly posted something about being raped as a child and his girlfriend was yelling at him about not being able to perform during a threesome. He is estranged from his family. He has told me that they're a little cuckoo so I allowed him to live here. His mom text me this morning. Super worried cuz he posted on Instagram so I ran out and talked to him and I need to respond to her to make sure that she is aware that he is either okay or I'm handling the situation but I'm trying not to get in the middle. Here is what I wrote her please rewrite it to be appropriate but understanding while not getting in the middle:

 😟 oh my goodness Tara, I am so sorry this is all happening, I too would be SO worried as a mom and I am a little worried now too. Carson has been doing really well (I thought) he got a new full-time job and has been going to church with us. I honestly had no idea what was or is going on with him about this. He doesn't tell me much. 

Rest assure the second I woke up and saw your text I ran out to talk to him and he was on his way to work. I stopped him and asked him if he was ok or what was going on and if he would talk to me about it and he said he just had a manic moment and he's fine now and not to worry. 

I've tried to stay neutral with all this due to him being an adult and wanting him to have a safe place here, but at this point I will be sitting him down when he gets home so I can make sure I am supporting him the way he needs. 

Donivan has a great older Christian male counselor that he has gone to this summer and if Carson is at that point or if I feel something else needs to be done I will insist that he sees him. 

Please know that I care so much for all these boys and am doing the best I can to make sure they are all ok. I do not support any estrangement when it comes to family, but I'm not able to make him do anything due to him being of age. But as soon as I am able to make an assessment when he gets home I'll make sure to let you know if he is ok.
